Answer: C
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 2) clearly shows the mass projecting over the posterior thoracic wall/spine, confirming a posterior location rather than anterior or midline. Because it is an extrapleural/chest wall lesion abutting the mediastinum rather than being within the lung parenchyma, it typically demonstrates a negative silhouette sign with mediastinal structures (preserving their borders), distinguishing it from intrapulmonary or true mediastinal masses.
